subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of cos²112½° − sin²52½°.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Apply the cos² − sin² identity
steps.margin_note: First mark. cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B) cos(A−B). Here A + B = 165° and A − B = 60°.
steps.memory_tip: cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B) cos(A−B). The two angles add to 165° and subtract to 60°.

recall.must_convey: That cos²A − sin²B = cos(A+B) cos(A−B) is applied, giving cos165° cos60°.
accept: use cos squared minus sin squared equals cos of the sum times cos of the difference
the angles add to one sixty five and subtract to sixty
apply the identity to get cos one sixty five cos sixty
identity apply cheste cos one sixty five cos sixty vasthundi
write it as cos one sixty five times cos sixty

steps.why: The first term is a cosine squared and the second a sine squared, so the expression is already in the form cos²A − sin²B. No conversion is needed before the formula.
common_mistakes: Using sin²A − sin²B, which needs both terms to be sines.
Writing the product as cos(A+B) sin(A−B).

steps.label: Substitute the exact values
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos165° = −cos15°, cos15° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2) and cos60° = ½. Multiply the three.
steps.memory_tip: cos165° = −cos15°, and cos15° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2). The minus sign is what makes the value negative.

recall.must_convey: That cos165° = −cos15°, and substituting cos15° = (√3 + 1)/(2√2) with cos60° = 1/2 gives −(√3 + 1)/(4√2).
accept: cos one sixty five is minus cos fifteen so the value is negative
cos fifteen is root three plus one over two root two and cos sixty is a half
multiply them to get minus root three plus one over four root two
cos one sixty five ante minus cos fifteen, so answer negative vasthundi
the answer is minus root three plus one by four root two

steps.why: 165° is a second quadrant angle, where the cosine is negative. That single minus sign is what makes the whole value negative.
common_mistakes: Losing the 1/2 that comes from cos60°.
